title: Agenteam — desktop agents
excerpt: The coding agent CLIs you already run, as characters that float above every window. Free for three agents.
content_html:
macOS · early access

Agents that live on your desktop.

Agenteam turns the coding agent CLIs you already run — Claude Code, Codex, opencode, pi — into little characters that float above every other window. Click one, say what you want, and it does the work in the folder you gave it.

Download for macOS Free for three agents. $9.9 lifts the cap for good — early-bird price, one payment. Bring your own agent CLI.

One agent per thing you care about.

It sits on top of everything

No window to find, no tab to switch to. An agent floats over whatever you are doing; click it and its chat balloon opens beside it, on whichever side of the screen has the room.

A folder of its own

Every agent works inside one workspace — a folder of its own, or a repo you point it at. The file tree lives right next to the conversation, so what it just wrote is one click away.

Things it does on its own

Ask for “every morning at nine” and the agent writes itself a routine. It runs on schedule, tells you what happened, and you can turn it off in the same place you set it up.

It keeps its memory

Each agent holds one long conversation across restarts. Talk to the balloon on the desktop or to the main window — same agent, same thread, same folder.

Your CLI. Your keys. Your machine.

Agenteam does not sell you tokens and does not run a model. It drives the agent CLI you have already installed and paid for, as a long-lived process on your own Mac.

  • pi

Conversations, settings and transcripts stay on your machine. Each agent runs with the permission mode you pick, inside the workspace you chose for it.

Free for three

  • Three agents
  • All four backends
  • Routines, workspaces, themes
  • Every update

Download Agenteam

macOS, signed and notarised.

Early bird

$9.9

One payment, no subscription. This is the early-access price and it goes up later; what you buy now stays bought.

  • As many agents as you like
  • Everything in the free app
  • Three Macs at a time

Buy a licence

Paste the key into Settings → Licence.

Why three?

Because three is enough to find out whether you want a fourth. One agent in your notes, one in a repo, one watching something — if that is your whole life, the free app is the whole product and you owe nothing.

Why so cheap?

Because it is early. Things are still moving, some backends are newer than others, and the price is what an early build is worth. It goes up when things settle.

Questions

Do I need an API key?
You need one of the agent CLIs installed and working in your terminal. Whatever signs you in there — a subscription, an API key — is what Agenteam uses. It adds no account of its own.
Which Mac?
Apple silicon and Intel, on a recent macOS. The app lives in the menu bar rather than the Dock. Windows and Linux are not there yet.
Where does my data go?
Nowhere we can see. The agents are child processes on your machine, and their transcripts sit in the app's own folder. What the CLI you chose sends to its model is between you and that CLI.
Can an agent touch the rest of my computer?
It runs in the workspace you give it, and the app warns you if you point one at your whole home folder. Permissions are per agent: ask before acting, plan only, or never ask.
What do I get without paying?
The whole app, with three agents. Not a trial: no clock, no nagging, every update. A licence only lifts the cap on how many agents you can keep at once.
How does the licence work?
After paying you land on a page with a key. Paste it into Settings → Licence; Agenteam checks it with us once, and from then on the check happens on your own machine. It never phones home again, and it works offline. Reopen that page any time to see the key again.
How many Macs?
Three at a time — a desktop, a laptop, and one more. When you stop using one, release it in Settings → Licence and the slot goes back. The key itself is yours for good.
Is the source open?
No. Agenteam is a closed-source app that drives open tools; what you download is the built, signed thing.
Something is broken.
Write to timqian@t9t.io — early on, that reaches the person who wrote the thing.

Put one on your desktop.

Download for macOS
